\chapter{Chapter03 — Decision Tree Fourier}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.SubspacesAndDecisionTrees.DecisionTreeFourier}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Expansion over decision tree paths]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b004
}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a finite list of paths, each assigning a
terminal output $a_p\in\mathbb{R}$ and a branch value in $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ or no
value at each coordinate. The path expansion is the function on
$(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n$ that sums, over $p\in P$, $a_p$ times the indicator that
the input follows the branch values assigned by $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expansion of the empty path list]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion_nil}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $n$, the path expansion of the empty list of real-output paths on
$n$ coordinates is the zero function on the length-$n$ vectors over $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Path expansion over a list cons]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion_cons}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a path on $n$ coordinates have a real output and
specify branch values at some coordinates. For any finite list of real-output paths, the
function obtained by summing each path's output times its indicator over the list formed
by placing the given path first is the sum of that path's output times its indicator and
the expansion of the remaining list.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation as a path expansion]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_pathExpansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_sum_pathIndicators_function, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a binary decision tree with real
outputs, whose queries are restricted to a set $I$ of the $n$ coordinates. For every
input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the evaluation of $T$ equals the sum, over all paths of $T$, of
the path's output multiplied by the indicator of the set of inputs matching that path's
queried coordinate values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decision tree path expansion]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.computes_eq_pathExpansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a decision tree on the $n$-dimensional binary cube have
real-valued leaves, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on that cube. If the tree
computes $f$, then $f$ equals the sum, over the tree's paths, of each path's output
multiplied by the indicator of the inputs matching that path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of the zero function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierCoeff_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every binary-cube vector $\gamma$, the vector Fourier
coefficient of the zero function at $\gamma$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a path expansion]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierCoeff_pathExpansion}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion_cons, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_add, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_const_mul}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P$ be a finite list of paths on the binary cube
with real outputs, and let $\gamma$ be a binary-cube vector. The vector Fourier
coefficient of the sum of the path outputs times their path indicators is the sum, over
the list, of each path output multiplied by the vector Fourier coefficient of its
indicator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier degree of a path expansion]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierDegree_pathExpansion_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.vectorFourierDegree_indicator_le_length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierCoeff_pathExpansion, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierDegree, FABL.vectorFourierDegree_le_iff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $P$ be a finite list of paths on the binary
cube with real outputs. If every path in $P$ fixes at most $k$ coordinates, then the
vector Fourier degree of the sum of their outputs times their path indicators is at most
$k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier degree bounded by decision tree depth]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierDegree_eval_le_depth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.path_length_le_depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierDegree_pathExpansion_le, FABL.vectorFourierDegree}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among the
$n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree indexed by $A$ with real-valued leaves.
The vector Fourier degree of the function computed by $T$ is at most the depth of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier degree of a computed function]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierDegree_le_depth_of_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierDegree_eval_le_depth, FABL.vectorFourierDegree}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among the
$n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree indexed by $A$. If $T$
computes a function $f$ from the binary cube to the reals, then the vector Fourier
degree of $f$ is at most the depth of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on path-length powers]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_two_pow_pathLength_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite list of paths on the $n$-coordinate Boolean cube, and let $k$ be a
nonnegative integer. If every path in the list has length at most $k$, then the sum of
$2^{\text{length}(p)}$ over the list is at most the length of the list times $2^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier sparsity bound by leaves and depth]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralSparsity_eval_le_leafCount_mul_two_pow_depth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval_eq_pathExpansion, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.path_length_le_depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralSparsity_pathExpansion_le_sum, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_two_pow_pathLength_le, FABL.spectralSparsity}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree on $n$
Boolean coordinates. The number of nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of the function
computed by $T$ is at most the number of leaves of $T$ multiplied by
$2^{\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree on $n$
Boolean coordinates. The number of nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of the function
computed by $T$ is at most $4^{\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Spectral sparsity bounds for decision trees]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralSparsity_le_of_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralSparsity_eval_le_four_pow_depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralSparsity_eval_le_leafCount_mul_two_pow_depth, FABL.spectralSparsity}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be a decision tree on the Boolean cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with real-valued
leaves, and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be the function it computes. The number
of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most both $L(T)2^{d(T)}$ and $4^{d(T)}$,
where $L(T)$ is the number of leaves and $d(T)$ is the depth of the tree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound for a sum over a list]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_map_le_length_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite list, let $w$ be a real-valued function on its element type, and let
$B$ be a real number. If $w(i)\le B$ for every element $i$ occurring in the list, then
the sum of $w(i)$ over the list is at most the length of the list times $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Path output bounded by function norm]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.abs_path_output_le_binaryFunctionInfinityNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.matches_base, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.computes_eq_path_output_of_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.abs_le_binaryFunctionInfinityNorm, FABL.binaryFunctionInfinityNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a decision tree on the $n$-dimensional binary cube with
real-valued leaves compute a function $f$ from that cube to $\mathbb R$, and let a path
occur in the tree's path list. Then the absolute value of the path's output is at most
$\sup_x |f(x)|$, where the supremum ranges over all inputs in the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leaf outputs bounded by the infinity norm]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_abs_pathOutput_le_leafCount_mul_infinityNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.abs_path_output_le_binaryFunctionInfinityNorm, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_map_le_length_mul, FABL.binaryFunctionInfinityNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree on the Boolean cube that computes $f$. The sum of
the absolute values of its leaf outputs is at most the number of leaves of $T$ times the
maximum of $|f(x)|$ over all inputs $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean coordinates
with real-valued leaves, and let $f$ be the function computed by $T$. The sum of the
absolute values of the vector Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most the product of the
supremum of $|f|$ on the Boolean cube and the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier norm bound by tree depth]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralPNorm_one_le_infinityNorm_mul_two_pow_depth_of_computes}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Computes, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount_le_two_pow_depth, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.spectralPNorm_one_le_infinityNorm_mul_leafCount_of_computes, FABL.binaryFunctionInfinityNorm, FABL.binaryFunctionInfinityNorm_nonneg, FABL.spectralPNorm}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p074-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean coordinates
with real-valued leaves, and let $f$ be the function computed by $T$. The sum of the
absolute values of the vector Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most the supremum of
$|f|$ on the Boolean cube multiplied by $2^{\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier granularity of a path indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.isVectorFourierGranular_intCast_mul_pathIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.isVectorFourierGranular_indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.IsVectorFourierGranular, FABL.IsVectorFourierGranular.intCast_mul, FABL.IsVectorFourierGranular.refine, FABL.inverse_two_pow_eq_natCast_mul_inverse_two_pow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P$ be a path on the Boolean cube with a real
output label, and suppose $\mathrm{length}(P)\le k$ for a nonnegative integer $k$. For
every integer $z$, the function equal to $z$ on the inputs matching the assignments of
$P$ and zero elsewhere has every Fourier coefficient on the sign cube equal to an
integer multiple of $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.F₂DecisionTree.isVectorFourierGranular_intCast_mul_pathIndicator}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let a finite list of paths on the $n$-coordinate binary cube
have real outputs. Suppose each path in the list has length at most $k$ and has an
integer output. Then every Fourier coefficient of the sign-cube function associated with
the sum of the paths' outputs times their path indicators is an integer multiple of
$2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the $n$-coordinate
binary cube with real outputs, and let $f$ be an integer-valued function on that cube.
If $T$ computes the real-valued function obtained from $f$, then every Fourier
coefficient of the corresponding function on the sign cube is an integer multiple of
$2^{-\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the path indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_one_of_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_zero_of_not_matches}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a path on the binary cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
specify a value in $\mathbb{F}_2$ at some coordinates, and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The
indicator of the set of points agreeing with every specified coordinate is nonnegative
at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected path indicator]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.expect_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePerpendicularCard_coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.support, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.coordinateZeroSubspace, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_of_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path assign either no value or a value in
$\bbr/2\bbr$ to each coordinate. Under the uniform probability measure on the binary
cube, the expected value of the indicator of the path’s cylinder is $2^{-\ell}$, where
$\ell$ is the number of coordinates assigned by the path.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sum of long-path indicators]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
Given a list of paths on $n$ binary coordinates and a natural number $k$, define a
real-valued function on the Boolean cube by summing, over the paths whose length exceeds
$k$, the indicator of each path.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the long-path indicator sum]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_nonneg, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let a finite list of paths on the $n$-coordinate binary cube be
given, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The sum, over listed paths of length greater
than $k$, of their path indicators at $x$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A matched long path contributes to the sum]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.one_le_longPathIndicatorSum_of_mem_of_matches}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.Matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_eq_one_of_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator_nonneg, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum_nonneg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathbb F_2^n$ be the set of length-$n$ vectors over
the two-element field, and let a path specify branch values at some coordinates and an
output label. For a finite list of such paths, a natural number $k$, and a vector
$x\in\mathbb F_2^n$, if a path in the list has more than $k$ specified coordinates and
its specified values agree with $x$, then the sum over the list of the indicators of the
paths with more than $k$ specified coordinates is at least $1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected sum of long-path indicators]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.expect_longPathIndicatorSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.expect_indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.indicator, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type, let $P$ be a finite list of paths
on $n$ coordinates, and let $k$ be a natural number. For a uniformly random input
$x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, the expected sum of the indicators of the paths in $P$ whose
lengths exceed $k$ equals the sum, over those paths, of $2^{-\ell}$, where $\ell$ is the
path length.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inverse path size bound]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.inversePathSize_le_inverseTwoPow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $P$ be a path specifying binary values at some of
the $n$ coordinates, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer no greater than the number of
coordinates specified by $P$. Then $2^{-\mathrm{length}(P)}\le 2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of inverse sizes over long paths]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_longPath_inversePathSize_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.inversePathSize_le_inverseTwoPow, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_map_le_length_mul}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite list of paths, where the length of a path is the number of
coordinates assigned along it, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. The sum of
$2^{-\text{length}(p)}$ over paths $p$ in the list with length greater than $k$ is at
most the length of the list times $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier weight above a degree threshold]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierWeightAbove}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂Support, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p069-b003}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $f:(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n\to\mathbb{R}$.
The Fourier weight of $f$ above degree $k$ is the sum of the squares of its vector
Fourier coefficients over all $\gamma\in(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^n$ whose support has
cardinality strictly greater than $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of Fourier weight above a threshold]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierWeightAbove_eq_fourierWeightAbove_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierWeightAbove, FABL.binaryFunctionOnSignCube, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAbove, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset_apply, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_fourierCoeff_binaryFunctionOnSignCube}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the binary
cube. The sum of squared vector Fourier coefficients of $f$ over indices whose support
has size greater than $k$ equals the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of the
corresponding function on the sign cube over subsets of size greater than $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linearity of the vector Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierCoeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on the binary cube,
and let $\gamma$ be a binary-cube vector. The vector Fourier coefficient of $f-g$ at
$\gamma$ equals the vector Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$ minus that of $g$ at
$\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier tail bounded by squared error]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierWeightAbove_le_expect_sq_sub_of_degree_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierCoeff_sub, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.vectorFourierWeightAbove, FABL.f₂Support, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierDegree, FABL.vectorFourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.vector_plancherel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued functions on the binary cube of dimension $n$, and let
$k$ be a nonnegative integer. If the Fourier degree of $g$ is at most $k$, then the sum
of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ on subsets of size greater than $k$ is
at most the uniform average of $(f(x)-g(x))^2$ over the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive leaf count]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount}
\difficulty{4}
Every decision tree on a finite set of coordinates has at least one leaf.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error bound for decision tree truncation]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.relativeHammingDist_eval_truncate_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.inversePathSize, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.Path.length, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.eval, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.exists_long_path_of_eval_truncate_ne, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.expect_longPathIndicatorSum, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.length_paths_eq_leafCount, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.longPathIndicatorSum_nonneg, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.one_le_longPathIndicatorSum_of_mem_of_matches, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.paths, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.sum_longPath_inversePathSize_le, FABL.F₂DecisionTree.truncate, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, and
let $T$ be a decision tree on the $n$ Boolean coordinates. For any fallback value
$a\in\alpha$ and any nonnegative integer $k$, the fraction of inputs on which $T$
differs from the tree obtained by replacing every query at truncation depth $k$ by $a$
is at most $L(T)2^{-k}$, where $L(T)$ is the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decision-tree truncation degree]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeTruncationDegree}
\leanok
For a natural number $s$ and a real number $\varepsilon$, define the truncation degree
to be the natural-number ceiling of $\log_2(s/\varepsilon)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Decision tree truncation degree bound]
\lean{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.mul_inverseTwoPow_decisionTreeTruncationDegree_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂DecisionTree.decisionTreeTruncationDegree}
\difficulty{4}
For a positive integer $s$ and a positive real number $\varepsilon$, let
$d=\left\lceil\log_2(s/\varepsilon)\right\rceil$. Then $s\,2^{-d}\leq\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, and
let $T$ be a decision tree querying Boolean coordinates among $n$ coordinates and
returning values in $\alpha$. For any fallback value $a\in\alpha$ and any real number
$\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of inputs in $\{0,1\}^n$ on which $T$ differs from the
tree obtained by truncating at depth
$\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(L/\varepsilon\bigr)\right\rceil$ and assigning $a$ at each
truncation point is at most $\varepsilon$, where $L$ is the number of leaves of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shallow approximation of decision trees]

\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, and let $T$
be a binary decision tree whose queries use coordinates from a fixed subset of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any fallback label in $\alpha$ and any real $\varepsilon>0$,
there is a tree $T'$ on the same available coordinates whose depth is at most
$\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(\operatorname{leafCount}(T)/\varepsilon\bigr)\right\rceil$, and
whose outputs disagree with those of $T$ on at most an $\varepsilon$ fraction of inputs
in $\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree on the Boolean cube, let $k$ be a nonnegative
integer, and suppose every value of $T$ is either $-1$ or $1$. For each input $x$, the
squared difference between the value of $T$ at $x$ and the value of the tree obtained by
truncating at depth $k$ and assigning value $0$ at newly created leaves is at most the
number of root-to-leaf paths of length greater than $k$ whose coordinate assignments
agree with $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be
a decision tree on $A$ with real outputs. Suppose $T(x)\in\{-1,1\}$ for every input
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$. For every natural number $k$, the expected squared difference between
$T(x)$ and the tree obtained by truncating $T$ at depth $k$ and assigning $0$ at
truncated leaves is at most the number of leaves of $T$ multiplied by $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

$\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. The sum of the squares of the
Fourier coefficients of its output function over all subsets of coordinates of size
greater than $k$ is at most the number of leaves of $T$ times $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$
coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $A$ with real outputs. Suppose that $f$
maps the binary cube on $n$ coordinates to $\bbr$, that $T$ computes $f$, and that $f$
takes only the values $-1$ and $1$. For $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, the sum of the squared
Fourier coefficients of the corresponding function on the sign cube, over all coordinate
sets $S$ whose size exceeds
$\left\lceil\log_2\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{leafCount}(T)}{\varepsilon}\right)\right\rceil$,
is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}
